question: What performance and responsiveness feedback do Essential PH-1 users give?
contexts: If you want a pure Android experience, get this phone!. If you are an Android enthusiast, then this phone is for you. It offers a pure Android experience without annoying bloatware and UI overlays found in do many other devices. I have used the Essential PH-1 now for two months and am very satisfied with my decision to go with it. Essential has pushed several updates to the platform that has enhanced performance and stability across nearly all aspects of the phone. The camera app has been greatly improved and performs extremely well compared to the early days of this phone. I have experienced ZERO crashes or feezes through the installed updates. In essence, I recommend the Essential Phone PH-1, especially if you want something different.

Beware of Essential and how it does business. I am extremely disappointed in the Essential PH-1 phone and the company's support model. I bought the PH-1 phone from Amazon who only sells it via third party resellers as Essential the company does not directly sell their phone through Amazon. Within two weeks, the PH-1 camera stops working so I contacted Essential for support. Keep in mind that Essential sells phones but does not have a phone number to contact them for support. They only communicate through email. I describe the problem to them and they request additional information from me: my name, address, proof of purchase, serial number, etc. After providing them with all the data, they inform me that they will not support me because I bought the phone from a reseller. They said they only support the phone if it is bought directly from Essential and Amazon.

I thought I was paying 3x what I normally pay for a phone to get one that WOULDN'T do this, but I was wrong. I took it in to my carrier who worked on it for about 30 minutes but agreed that it was a problem with the phone itself, not the SIM Card. Even better, I emailed Essential about the problem with no response. Thankfully, the return policy on Amazon allowed me to return it and get a full refund; I used the money to buy a brand-new S7 for less than the PH-1 costs. I would recommend a Galaxy S7-S9 more than I will ever recommend the Essential PH-1. Bottom Line: if you're willing to risk a manufacturing problem with a company that is unstable, go for it.

Also bear in mind a lot of reviewers tend to parrot older criticisms that predate Essentials many updates. It's quite conceivable that with everything Essential is doing, in a month or two Essential Phone PH-1 could well be as good or better than many of its $1000 competitors.
